The disclosure discipline is followed correctly - disclosed=yes, label READ, capped at S3, and the finding says so in the disclosure field; READ is right here even though the cost figures are data-derived, because the COMMON_RULES disclosure clause forces READ. All ledger figures reproduce exactly on my own read-only pass of live ledgers/evidence.jsonl (2026-09-03T07:04Z, UNANCHORED): 70 `low` attempts under digest 7e6f3d68, mean 0.03735 USD, mean 3110 reasoning tokens, 53 of 70 stored (76 percent), mean latency 31.5 s; 432 x mean = 16.13 USD, 432 x 70/53 x mean = 21.31 USD, 365-day version 13.63 to 18.00 USD; whole-ledger total 6.9377835 USD. TWO CORRECTIONS REQUIRED, both in my lens. (1) 'What is not disclosed is the *cost*' is false: the authors published a cost projection for a full `low` run in Amendment 2 - 'The safety budget is 80 percent of the remaining cap, 7.9756 USD. `low` projects 11.7812 USD and fails it.' (REGISTRATION.md:476-477) - and sized the 365-day variant's power at :488-490. Rewrite to: the authors DID price and reject `low` at Amendment 2 (11.7812 USD, pre-Amendment-4 schema, against the then-remaining cap); what the closure's cost section omits is any restatement of that route under the in-force schema and against the 3.0622 USD now unspent. Add :476-477 to disclosure_ref. (2) The report summary's phrase 'omitting the ~16 to 21 USD variant the registration itself named, with 3.0622 USD unspent under the cap' invites the inference that the unspent balance could fund it; 16 to 21 USD exceeds both the 3.0622 USD remaining and the whole 10.00 USD cap. The finding body concedes this ('The binding blocker is the leftover balance'), so make the summary say it too - otherwise the closure's 'No model has one' reads as more evasive than the arithmetic supports.
